questions.text: State and explain Brewer's CAP Theorem (Consistency, Availability, Partition Tolerance). Explain why a distributed system can guarantee at most two of the three properties under network partitions. Compare Strong Consistency, Sequential Consistency, and Eventual Consistency.

Explain the architecture of Remote Procedure Call (RPC) and Java RMI. Describe the roles of Client Stub, Server Stub, Parameter Marshalling, and Dispatcher. Compare At-Least-Once, At-Most-Once, and Exactly-Once delivery semantics.

Compare Cloud Service Models: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Software as a Service (SaaS) with shared responsibility architectural diagrams. Compare Public, Private, Hybrid, and Community cloud deployment models.

Explain Cloud Virtualization techniques: Full Virtualization, Paravirtualization, and Hardware-Assisted Virtualization. Compare Hypervisor-based Virtual Machines (VMs) with OS-level Containerization (Docker) in terms of isolation, resource overhead, startup latency, and density.
What is a Web Service? Why is RESTful web service more popular than SOAP-based web service in today's distributed application development? Explain with real-world examples.
How is Enterprise Application Integration different from legacy middleware systems? Explain the benefits of N-tier distributed architecture over monolithic architecture in software development.
Describe the mechanism of database connection pooling in high-traffic enterprise applications. What are the major considerations for creating and sizing an efficient connection pool?
What is Inversion of Control (IoC)? Explain the different techniques how Dependency Injection (DI) is implemented in distributed application frameworks.
Explain Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) concepts and design principles. Compare Service-Oriented Architecture with Microservices architecture in distributed cloud deployments.
Explain Enterprise Java Beans (EJB) architecture with its importance. List out the differences between Session Beans (Stateless, Stateful, Singleton) and Message-Driven Beans.
Explain Clock Synchronization in distributed systems: Lamport's Logical Clocks and Vector Clocks. Prove that if event $a$ happened-before event $b$ ($a \to b$), then $C(a) < C(b)$.
Explain Election Algorithms in distributed systems: (a) The Bully Algorithm, and (b) The Ring Election Algorithm. Trace message exchanges and state updates when the current coordinator node crashes.
Explain the Two-Phase Commit (2PC) atomic transaction protocol in distributed systems. Describe the Voting Phase, Commit Phase, and coordinator recovery mechanisms under failure.

questions.chapter: Cloud Storage and Big Data Frameworks
questions.text: Explain the architecture of the Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS): NameNode, DataNodes, Secondary NameNode, chunk block replication ($128\text{ MB}$), and rack awareness. Explain the MapReduce distributed computational model with WordCount dataflow.
Write short notes on: (a) Edge Computing versus Cloud Computing, (b) Facade Design Pattern in enterprise tiers, (c) Web 3.0 and data decentralization.

Explain Elasticity and Auto-Scaling in cloud infrastructure. Differentiate between Horizontal Scaling (Scale-Out/Scale-In) and Vertical Scaling (Scale-Up/Scale-Down). Describe live virtual machine migration.
